modelingNotes: Petra's, Plaza Midwood, Charlotte (bar and live-music venue since 2007, 1917–1919 Commonwealth Avenue) — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/petras.ts

Map frame: x east, y north, z up, metres, placed at bearing 358°: the model's +y runs back from the parking strip on Commonwealth Avenue, so the shopfront is the model's south face. The anchor is the metre-based centroid of the OSM outline (way/323192880, height 5), an L: the full-width front room and a narrower rear wing on the east side. The walls follow it. Both side walls are party walls in a row of one-storey shops.

A small venue is its front: red-brown brick with a plain coping, a flat dark metal canopy across the whole shopfront, teal-framed shop windows either side of a teal door, and the 2026 sign above the canopy: a teal rounded-end board with a coral underline that runs past its right end (drawn without the script lettering).

Measured: the outline (OSM) and the heights, from the USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016 lidar (0.5 m DSM sampled in this frame, above the front's west corner, the lowest ground): the front parapet 4.4 m, the other parapets 4.2 m, the roof 3.6 m at the front to 4.0 m at the back (drawn flat at 3.8 m). OSM's height=5 is a rounded tag the lidar doesn't bear out. Estimated: the shopfront, canopy and sign sizes and positions, from two front photos, scaled down with the front. Invented: the rear wing's walls, which no photo shows, are plain brick. No licensed exterior photo exists (Commons, Openverse, Mapillary), so the front and colours rest on look-only references.

Rework (2026-10): heights brought down from 5.0/5.1 m to the lidar; the form, the sign and the colours are the earlier model's. Doubt: the 2016 lidar shows a canopy about 1 m deep at roughly 4 m, higher than the 2026 photo's canopy under the sign; the canopy was probably replaced with the sign, so the photo's arrangement is kept.

The DEM rises 0.5 m along the front from west to east and 1.1 m to the rear, so y = 0 is the front's west corner; the shopfront starts at the east end's ground and runs into the ground at the west end.

References: USGS NAIP aerial (public domain) for the footprint and the flat roof. Look-only: CLTure's photos of the front, "Petra's prepares for grand reopening" (clture.org/petras, July 2021: brick, sign position, shopfront bays) and "Petra's is adapting to the times" (clture.org/ petras-vintage-little-shop-of-petras, Feb 2026: the teal sign, canopy and teal frames). Mapillary has no view of the front.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "petras", model "petras"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/petras.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
